svg.title: An affine modular trace orbit closes on one graph
svg.desc: The transported fundamental derivation is delta plus i times t times psi. In cochain coordinates delta and i psi its exact affine orbit is the line with coordinates one and t, shown for t from minus two to two. These coordinates do not assert a dual-space norm. Its normalized first derivative is psi and its second derivative is zero. The lower panel closes the single simultaneous core graph of delta, psi and the normalized generator D. The resulting complete domain F is matrix inverse closed and represents all ambient K-theory. Its flow bound is one plus the absolute value of t. Contraction i_D psi is the circle logarithmic two-cocycle, and the universal inserted-coefficient expression contains only ambient norms of x and y.
svg.metadata: Original CC0 figure. Lemma 13.23, Corollary 13.24, equations 13.81-13.84 and Exercises 7.28-7.29. Human source: Connes 1986 Lemmas 7.4-7.6 and Remark 7.16(b). The simultaneous closed graph proof is authored locally. Cochain coordinates are an affine schematic, not a metric, projection or numerical dual-space sample. Exact parameter samples: t=-2,-1,0,1,2.
svg.text: The modular orbit is affine; its contraction uses one common domain
Exact cochain identity: 𝒯ₜδ = δ + t(iψ). Normalization: D = (1/i) dσₜ/dt at t = 0.
Coordinates show no norm or inner product on B*.
b ∈ E ∩ Dom D, dense in B
Normalized contraction: τ = iDψ = τw on the circle
∫τ x da y db = ψ(a)(y D(b) x) − ψ(b)(x D(a) y)
Only a and b are differentiated. The resulting two-trace pairs with every K₀(B) class.
Lemma 13.23; Corollary 13.24; Exercises 7.28–7.29. Purely C*-algebraic data with explicit graph domains.
